To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# sequence-engine
2	
3	Small sequence model engine with explicit truncated backpropagation, written so that truncation points and hidden-state resets are observable from the public API.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m sequence_engine --selftest
16	
17	The built-in self-check runs only in memory (including the incremental
18	checkpoint path) and writes no files.
19	
20	## Public interface
21	
22	`sequence_engine.Tensor(data)` and `sequence_engine.Sequential(modules)`.
23	- `Tensor.tolist() -> list`, `Tensor.shape -> list[int]`.
24	- `Sequential.forward(batch, hidden=None) -> (output, hidden)`.
25	- `Sequential.backward(loss) -> None` accumulates gradients.
26	  `loss` is a scalar/Tensor seed or the tuple form `(output, upstream)`
27	  carrying the exact Tensor returned by the preceding `forward`.
28	  Calling `backward` without a preceding `forward`, or twice for one
29	  `forward`, raises `RuntimeError`. If a layer raises mid-pass the partial
30	  gradients are rolled back and the same `backward` may be retried; a retry
31	  is not a second backward.
32	- `Sequential.zero_grad() -> None` clears accumulated gradients.
33	- `Sequential.update(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place step
34	  `theta <- theta - learning_rate * grad` on every parameter. Gradients are
35	  not cleared; parameters without a gradient are unchanged. A non-finite or
36	  non-numeric learning rate raises `ValueError`.
37	- `Sequential.adam_step(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place Adam
38	  step with coefficients fixed by the engine (they are not parameters of
39	  the call and the optimizer kind cannot be swapped): moments are updated
40	  as `m <- 0.9*m + 0.1*g` and `v <- 0.999*v + 0.001*g^2`, the step count
41	  `t` starts at 1 on the first call and increments by one each call, and
42	  the parameter update is
43	  `theta <- theta - lr * (m/(1-0.9^t)) / (sqrt(v/(1-0.999^t)) + 1e-8)`.
44	  Parameters without a gradient are unchanged but `t` still advances;
45	  gradients are not cleared. The one-step `update`, gradient accumulation
46	  and `zero_grad` semantics are unchanged and the two optimizer paths do
47	  not share any state besides the parameters. A non-finite or non-numeric
48	  learning rate raises `ValueError`; an unstepped state starts at `t = 0`
49	  with zero moments.
50	- `Sequential.set_recompute(enabled) -> None` switches bounded-memory mode
51	  on or off. With it on, a `forward` keeps only the slice-boundary hidden
52	  state plus a few anchors (the segment input and the incoming hidden
53	  values); the matching `backward` recomputes the activations from those
54	  anchors, so retained activation memory stays bounded by the segment
55	  size instead of growing with the total sequence length. Forward
56	  outputs and parameter gradients are bitwise identical with the switch
57	  on or off. The switch may only be flipped between segments; flipping it
58	  while a backward is pending raises `RuntimeError` without touching the
59	  container. If a parameter is rewritten while a recompute segment is in
60	  flight, `backward` raises `RuntimeError` before any gradient is
61	  accumulated (no half state; the failed pass does not consume the
62	  forward and may be retried on a fresh forward).
63	- `Sequential.parameters() -> list[Tensor]` in registration order.
64	- `Sequential.save(target) -> None` fixes parameters, accumulated gradients
65	  (zeros for parameters that have none), the optimizer state (Adam first
66	  and second moments and step count; zero moments and `t = 0` when
67	  `adam_step` has never run), the slice-boundary hidden state and the
68	  layer order in one versioned binary checkpoint. `target` is a
69	  filesystem path (`str`/`os.PathLike`), an existing directory used as an
70	  incremental checkpoint chain, a `MemoryChain`, or an in-memory
71	  `bytearray`; saving mutates no existing state and repeated saves of the
72	  same state produce identical bytes. A boundary exists before the first
73	  segment and after every `forward` -- the hidden state returned by that
74	  forward *is* the boundary -- so saving is allowed even when the latest
75	  forward has not been back-propagated yet; the snapshot fixes the boundary
76	  state, not the in-flight activations.
77	- `Sequential.load(source) -> hidden | None` restores a checkpoint from a
78	  path, an incremental-chain directory, a `MemoryChain`, or bytes-like
79	  buffer and returns the restored hidden-state list for the next
80	  `forward(batch, hidden)`. The format version (the previous format
81	  versions 1 and 2 are read and migrated item by item; a migrated
82	  optimizer state starts at `t = 0` with zero moments;
83	  `Sequential.loaded_from_version` reports the version a successful load
84	  came from), every tensor shape and the layer order (count, layer
85	  kinds, per-layer parameter shapes) are checked first; hidden-state
86	  shapes are verified on the spot, even for a model that has never run a
87	  forward. Any mismatch, truncation, corruption or missing field rejects
88	  the whole checkpoint with `ValueError` -- nothing is partially applied
89	  or silently filled in. A missing path raises `FileNotFoundError`.
90	
91	### Threading
92	
93	All `Sequential` operations are serialised by one per-container lock, so
94	multiple threads may interleave `forward`, `backward`, `update`,
95	`adam_step`, `save` and `load`. Under any interleaving each parameter's
96	final value is one a serial execution of the same calls could have
97	produced: `update` and `adam_step` each apply as one atomic step, a
98	`load` is never observed half-applied, and no `save` can read a
99	half-written tensor (optimizer moments included). Every snapshot
100	corresponds to one complete slice boundary -- never two passes half
101	mixed. When two threads save to the same file path the bytes on disk are
102	always one or the other writer's complete checkpoint (never a blend).
103	
104	## Checkpoint file semantics
105	
106	Path saves are atomic: bytes go to a temporary file in the destination
107	directory, which is `os.replace`d over any existing file (no backup is
108	kept). A process killed mid-write leaves only the rejected temporary file;
109	the final path either holds the previous complete checkpoint or the new
110	one. A half-written or corrupted file at the load path is detected by its
111	trailer and CRC and refused with `ValueError`.
112	
113	Floats are stored as raw IEEE-754 float64 values, so a save/load round-trip
114	is bitwise identical, including the sign of negative zero. Integers must
115	fit in int64 (the Adam step count included) and all serialized numbers
116	must be finite; oversized integers or non-finite floats raise
117	`ValueError` on save -- optimizer moments with such values can never
118	enter a checkpoint -- and a payload that merely contains an oversized or
119	non-finite value is refused on load. Saving into a directory that does
120	not exist or is not writable, or failing because the disk is full,
121	raises `OSError`; the caller chooses the destination path.
122	
123	## Checkpoint format versions
124	
125	The on-disk format is versioned. This build writes **version 3** and
126	still reads **versions 1 and 2**: an old file is migrated item by item
127	into the current document shape and the source version is recorded; if
128	migration fails on any item the whole file is rejected rather than
129	silently filled in. Version 3 adds the optimizer state (Adam first/second
130	moments and step count); a version-1 or version-2 checkpoint has no such
131	state and migrates to `t = 0` with zero moments. A file with an unknown
132	version, or a header with a field added or removed, is rejected with
133	`ValueError`. A migrated state re-saves as native version 3. Unknown
134	(future) versions are never guessed; they are refused.
135	
136	## Incremental checkpoint chains
137	
138	Passing an existing directory (or a `MemoryChain`) to `save`/`load` uses an
139	incremental chain instead of one self-contained file:
140	
141	- the first save writes a full **basis** segment (`seg-0000000000.seqd`);
142	- every later save appends a delta segment naming only the tensors that
143	  changed, compared by encoded leaf identity (so float sign bits such as
144	  `-0.0` count); unchanged saves append an empty delta deterministically,
145	  and layers with no parameters participate like any other layer;
146	- a `head` pointer names the newest committed segment. Each segment file is
147	  written completely and atomically before the head is advanced, so a crash,
148	  a full disk or two saves racing into one directory always leave a single
149	  complete chain reachable from `head`.
150	
151	Loading walks the basis and every delta up to the head and reassembles the
152	state by layer (parameters, gradients, optimizer moments and step count,
153	then hidden slots). The reassembled state is bit for bit identical to
154	the full snapshot taken at the same moment, including a chain written by
155	the previous version-2 engine: old deltas are read, their hidden indices
156	remapped, and the missing optimizer state filled in from the starting
157	values. Any segment in the chain that is truncated, corrupt, missing a
158	field, out of order, changes the layer order or parameter/shapes, or
159	introduces hidden state incompletely makes the load reject the **whole**
160	chain with `ValueError`. A missing chain directory or a referenced
161	segment file that is absent raises `FileNotFoundError`; an unwritable
162	directory or a full disk raises `OSError`. A chain cannot change the
163	model's layer order or parameter shapes -- use a fresh full snapshot for
164	a different model.
165	
166	`MemoryChain` (exported from `sequence_engine`) is an in-memory chain with
167	identical commit semantics, useful for tests and long-running processes that
168	want incremental snapshots without files.
169	
170	## Tests
171	
172	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
173	
174	## Limits
175	
176	CPU only; no GPU backend.
177	One backward pass per forward pass.
178	The engine trains nothing on its own and ships no dataset.
179

# sequence-engine

Small sequence model engine with explicit truncated backpropagation, written so that truncation points and hidden-state resets are observable from the public API.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m sequence_engine --selftest

The built-in self-check runs only in memory (including the incremental
checkpoint path) and writes no files.

## Public interface

`sequence_engine.Tensor(data)` and `sequence_engine.Sequential(modules)`.
- `Tensor.tolist() -> list`, `Tensor.shape -> list[int]`.
- `Sequential.forward(batch, hidden=None) -> (output, hidden)`.
- `Sequential.backward(loss) -> None` accumulates gradients.
  `loss` is a scalar/Tensor seed or the tuple form `(output, upstream)`
  carrying the exact Tensor returned by the preceding `forward`.
  Calling `backward` without a preceding `forward`, or twice for one
  `forward`, raises `RuntimeError`. If a layer raises mid-pass the partial
  gradients are rolled back and the same `backward` may be retried; a retry
  is not a second backward.
- `Sequential.zero_grad() -> None` clears accumulated gradients.
- `Sequential.update(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place step
  `theta <- theta - learning_rate * grad` on every parameter. Gradients are
  not cleared; parameters without a gradient are unchanged. A non-finite or
  non-numeric learning rate raises `ValueError`.
- `Sequential.adam_step(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place Adam
  step with coefficients fixed by the engine (they are not parameters of
  the call and the optimizer kind cannot be swapped): moments are updated
  as `m <- 0.9*m + 0.1*g` and `v <- 0.999*v + 0.001*g^2`, the step count
  `t` starts at 1 on the first call and increments by one each call, and
  the parameter update is
  `theta <- theta - lr * (m/(1-0.9^t)) / (sqrt(v/(1-0.999^t)) + 1e-8)`.
  Parameters without a gradient are unchanged but `t` still advances;
  gradients are not cleared. The one-step `update`, gradient accumulation
  and `zero_grad` semantics are unchanged and the two optimizer paths do
  not share any state besides the parameters. A non-finite or non-numeric
  learning rate raises `ValueError`; an unstepped state starts at `t = 0`
  with zero moments.
- `Sequential.set_recompute(enabled) -> None` switches bounded-memory mode
  on or off. With it on, a `forward` keeps only the slice-boundary hidden
  state plus a few anchors (the segment input and the incoming hidden
  values); the matching `backward` recomputes the activations from those
  anchors, so retained activation memory stays bounded by the segment
  size instead of growing with the total sequence length. Forward
  outputs and parameter gradients are bitwise identical with the switch
  on or off. The switch may only be flipped between segments; flipping it
  while a backward is pending raises `RuntimeError` without touching the
  container. If a parameter is rewritten while a recompute segment is in
  flight, `backward` raises `RuntimeError` before any gradient is
  accumulated (no half state; the failed pass does not consume the
  forward and may be retried on a fresh forward).
- `Sequential.parameters() -> list[Tensor]` in registration order.
- `Sequential.save(target) -> None` fixes parameters, accumulated gradients
  (zeros for parameters that have none), the optimizer state (Adam first
  and second moments and step count; zero moments and `t = 0` when
  `adam_step` has never run), the slice-boundary hidden state and the
  layer order in one versioned binary checkpoint. `target` is a
  filesystem path (`str`/`os.PathLike`), an existing directory used as an
  incremental checkpoint chain, a `MemoryChain`, or an in-memory
  `bytearray`; saving mutates no existing state and repeated saves of the
  same state produce identical bytes. A boundary exists before the first
  segment and after every `forward` -- the hidden state returned by that
  forward *is* the boundary -- so saving is allowed even when the latest
  forward has not been back-propagated yet; the snapshot fixes the boundary
  state, not the in-flight activations.
- `Sequential.load(source) -> hidden | None` restores a checkpoint from a
  path, an incremental-chain directory, a `MemoryChain`, or bytes-like
  buffer and returns the restored hidden-state list for the next
  `forward(batch, hidden)`. The format version (the previous format
  versions 1 and 2 are read and migrated item by item; a migrated
  optimizer state starts at `t = 0` with zero moments;
  `Sequential.loaded_from_version` reports the version a successful load
  came from), every tensor shape and the layer order (count, layer
  kinds, per-layer parameter shapes) are checked first; hidden-state
  shapes are verified on the spot, even for a model that has never run a
  forward. Any mismatch, truncation, corruption or missing field rejects
  the whole checkpoint with `ValueError` -- nothing is partially applied
  or silently filled in. A missing path raises `FileNotFoundError`.

### Threading

All `Sequential` operations are serialised by one per-container lock, so
multiple threads may interleave `forward`, `backward`, `update`,
`adam_step`, `save` and `load`. Under any interleaving each parameter's
final value is one a serial execution of the same calls could have
produced: `update` and `adam_step` each apply as one atomic step, a
`load` is never observed half-applied, and no `save` can read a
half-written tensor (optimizer moments included). Every snapshot
corresponds to one complete slice boundary -- never two passes half
mixed. When two threads save to the same file path the bytes on disk are
always one or the other writer's complete checkpoint (never a blend).

## Checkpoint file semantics

Path saves are atomic: bytes go to a temporary file in the destination
directory, which is `os.replace`d over any existing file (no backup is
kept). A process killed mid-write leaves only the rejected temporary file;
the final path either holds the previous complete checkpoint or the new
one. A half-written or corrupted file at the load path is detected by its
trailer and CRC and refused with `ValueError`.

Floats are stored as raw IEEE-754 float64 values, so a save/load round-trip
is bitwise identical, including the sign of negative zero. Integers must
fit in int64 (the Adam step count included) and all serialized numbers
must be finite; oversized integers or non-finite floats raise
`ValueError` on save -- optimizer moments with such values can never
enter a checkpoint -- and a payload that merely contains an oversized or
non-finite value is refused on load. Saving into a directory that does
not exist or is not writable, or failing because the disk is full,
raises `OSError`; the caller chooses the destination path.

## Checkpoint format versions

The on-disk format is versioned. This build writes **version 3** and
still reads **versions 1 and 2**: an old file is migrated item by item
into the current document shape and the source version is recorded; if
migration fails on any item the whole file is rejected rather than
silently filled in. Version 3 adds the optimizer state (Adam first/second
moments and step count); a version-1 or version-2 checkpoint has no such
state and migrates to `t = 0` with zero moments. A file with an unknown
version, or a header with a field added or removed, is rejected with
`ValueError`. A migrated state re-saves as native version 3. Unknown
(future) versions are never guessed; they are refused.

## Incremental checkpoint chains

Passing an existing directory (or a `MemoryChain`) to `save`/`load` uses an
incremental chain instead of one self-contained file:

- the first save writes a full **basis** segment (`seg-0000000000.seqd`);
- every later save appends a delta segment naming only the tensors that
  changed, compared by encoded leaf identity (so float sign bits such as
  `-0.0` count); unchanged saves append an empty delta deterministically,
  and layers with no parameters participate like any other layer;
- a `head` pointer names the newest committed segment. Each segment file is
  written completely and atomically before the head is advanced, so a crash,
  a full disk or two saves racing into one directory always leave a single
  complete chain reachable from `head`.

Loading walks the basis and every delta up to the head and reassembles the
state by layer (parameters, gradients, optimizer moments and step count,
then hidden slots). The reassembled state is bit for bit identical to
the full snapshot taken at the same moment, including a chain written by
the previous version-2 engine: old deltas are read, their hidden indices
remapped, and the missing optimizer state filled in from the starting
values. Any segment in the chain that is truncated, corrupt, missing a
field, out of order, changes the layer order or parameter/shapes, or
introduces hidden state incompletely makes the load reject the **whole**
chain with `ValueError`. A missing chain directory or a referenced
segment file that is absent raises `FileNotFoundError`; an unwritable
directory or a full disk raises `OSError`. A chain cannot change the
model's layer order or parameter shapes -- use a fresh full snapshot for
a different model.

`MemoryChain` (exported from `sequence_engine`) is an in-memory chain with
identical commit semantics, useful for tests and long-running processes that
want incremental snapshots without files.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

CPU only; no GPU backend.
One backward pass per forward pass.
The engine trains nothing on its own and ships no dataset.

331	def _frame(magic, end_magic, header, payload):
332	    header_bytes = json.dumps(
333	        header, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True
334	    ).encode("utf-8")
335	
336	    body = bytearray()
337	    body += magic
338	    body += struct.pack("<I", header["v"])
339	    body += struct.pack("<Q", len(header_bytes))
340	    body += header_bytes
341	    crc = zlib.crc32(header_bytes)
342	    leaf_count = 0
343	    for chunk in payload:
344	        body += chunk
345	        crc = zlib.crc32(chunk, crc)
346	        leaf_count += 1
347	    body += end_magic
348	    body += struct.pack("<Q", leaf_count)
349	    body += struct.pack("<I", crc & 0xFFFFFFFF)
350	    return bytes(body)

359	    def __init__(self, payload):
360	        self._payload = payload

363	    def _leaf(self):
364	        tag = self._payload[self._pos]
365	        chunk = self._payload[self._pos + 1 : self._pos + 9]
366	        self._pos += 9
367	        if tag == _TAG_INT:
368	            value = struct.unpack("<q", chunk)[0]
369	            return value
370	        if tag == _TAG_FLOAT:
371	            value = struct.unpack("<d", chunk)[0]
372	            if not math.isfinite(value):
373	                raise CheckpointError(
374	                    "checkpoint payload contains a non-finite floating value"
375	                )
376	            return value
377	        raise CheckpointError(f"unknown leaf tag {tag!r} in payload")
378	
379	    def tree(self, shape):
380	        if not shape:
381	            return self._leaf()
382	        return [self.tree(shape[1:]) for _ in range(shape[0])]
383	
384	    def remaining(self):
385	        return (len(self._payload) - self._pos) // 9

388	def _read_frame(data, magic, end_magic, what):
389	    prefix_len = len(magic) + 4 + 8
390	    if len(data) < prefix_len:
391	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} is truncated while reading its header")
392	    if data[: len(magic)] != magic:
393	        raise CheckpointError(f"not a {what} (bad magic)")
394	    (version,) = struct.unpack("<I", data[len(magic) : len(magic) + 4])
395	    (header_len,) = struct.unpack(
396	        "<Q", data[len(magic) + 4 : len(magic) + 4 + 8]
397	    )
398	    if header_len <= 0:
399	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header length is invalid")
400	
401	    trailer_pos = data.rfind(end_magic)
402	    trailer_len = len(end_magic) + 8 + 4
403	    if trailer_pos < 0 or len(data) - trailer_pos != trailer_len:
404	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} trailer is missing or the file is torn")
405	    header_start = prefix_len
406	    payload_end = trailer_pos
407	    if header_len > payload_end - header_start:
408	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header overruns the payload area")
409	    header_bytes = data[header_start : header_start + header_len]
410	
411	    (leaf_count, stored_crc) = struct.unpack(
412	        "<QI", data[trailer_pos + len(end_magic) :]
413	    )
414	    actual_crc = zlib.crc32(data[header_start:payload_end])
415	    if actual_crc != stored_crc:
416	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} CRC mismatch: the file is corrupt or torn")
417	
418	    try:
419	        header = json.loads(header_bytes.decode("utf-8"))
420	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
421	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header is invalid: {exc}") from exc
422	    if not isinstance(header, dict):
423	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header must be a JSON object")
424	    if header.get("v") != version:
425	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header version does not match its frame")
426	
427	    payload = data[header_start + header_len : payload_end]
428	    if len(payload) != leaf_count * 9:
429	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} payload has the wrong size")

456	    if not isinstance(header["v"], int) or isinstance(header["v"], bool):

473	        raise CheckpointError("layer order must be a non-empty list")

478	            raise CheckpointError(f"layer {index} kind must be a non-empty string")

484	        raise CheckpointError(
485	            "layer order/parameter shapes do not match the parameter tensor list"
486	        )
487	    if not isinstance(header["pending"], bool):
488	        raise CheckpointError("pending flag must be a boolean")

492	def parse_bytes(raw):
493	    """Validate and decode a full snapshot (v1, v2 or v3); return the document.
494	
495	    A version-1 or version-2 file is migrated item by item into the current
496	    document shape (a missing optimizer state starts at ``t = 0`` with zero
497	    moments).  Any failure while migrating rejects the whole file -- nothing
498	    is partially returned or filled in.  The document itself carries no
499	    source-version field; use :func:`load_bytes_with_source` when the
500	    originating format version is needed.
501	    """
502	    document, _source = _decode_full(raw)
503	    return document

506	def load_bytes_with_source(source):
507	    """Like :func:`load_bytes`, also returning the source format version."""
508	    if isinstance(source, MemoryChain):
509	        document = load_chain_memory(source)
510	        return document, FORMAT_VERSION
511	    if isinstance(source, (str, os.PathLike)):
512	        path = os.fspath(source)
513	        if os.path.isdir(path):
514	            return load_chain(path), FORMAT_VERSION
515	        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
516	            raw = fh.read()
517	        return _decode_full(raw)
518	    if isinstance(source, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
519	        return _decode_full(source)
520	    raise TypeError("load source must be a path or bytes")

522	
523	def _decode_full(raw):
524	    """Return ``(document, source_version)`` for one full snapshot."""
525	    if not isinstance(raw, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
526	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must be bytes")
527	    data = bytes(raw)
528	    version, header, payload, leaf_count = _read_frame(
529	        data, MAGIC, END_MAGIC, "checkpoint"
530	    )
531	    if version not in SUPPORTED_READ_VERSIONS:
532	        raise CheckpointError(
533	            f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; this build reads "
534	            f"versions {SUPPORTED_READ_VERSIONS}"
535	        )
536	    param_shapes, hidden_shapes, optim_t = _parse_full_header(header, version)
537	
538	    param_leaves = sum(_shape_size(shape) for shape in param_shapes)
539	    total_leaves = param_leaves * 2
540	    if hidden_shapes is not None:
541	        total_leaves += sum(_shape_size(shape) for shape in hidden_shapes)
542	    if optim_t is not None:
543	        total_leaves += param_leaves * 2
544	    if total_leaves != leaf_count:
545	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint leaf count does not match the header")
546	
547	    reader = _LeafReader(payload)
548	    params = [{"s": shape, "v": reader.tree(shape)} for shape in param_shapes]
549	    grads = [{"s": shape, "v": reader.tree(shape)} for shape in param_shapes]
550	    hidden = (
551	        None
552	        if hidden_shapes is None
553	        else [{"s": shape, "v": reader.tree(shape)} for shape in hidden_shapes]
554	    )
555	    if optim_t is not None:
556	        optim = {
557	            "t": optim_t,
558	            "m": [{"s": shape, "v": reader.tree(shape)} for shape in param_shapes],
559	            "v": [{"s": shape, "v": reader.tree(shape)} for shape in param_shapes],
560	        }
561	    else:
562	        optim = None
563	    if reader.remaining() != 0:
564	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint payload has trailing bytes")
565	
566	    document = {
567	        "params": params,
568	        "grads": grads,
569	        "hidden": hidden,
570	        "optim": optim,
571	        "layers": [
572	            {"kind": layer["kind"], "shapes": [list(s) for s in layer["shapes"]]}
573	            for layer in header["layers"]
574	        ],
575	        "pending": header["pending"],
576	    }
577	    if version == 1:
578	        document = _migrate_v1_document(document)
579	    if version < FORMAT_VERSION:
580	        document = _migrate_add_optim(document)
581	    return document, version

584	def _migrate_v1_document(document):
585	    """Migrate a decoded version-1 document item by item.
586	
587	    The tensor semantics are shared across versions, so migration is a
588	    field-by-field re-validation rather than a guess: every tensor, shape
589	    and descriptor is copied and checked individually.  A failure on any
590	    item raises and the caller rejects the whole file.  The optimizer
591	    state, absent before version 3, is filled in separately by
592	    :func:`_migrate_add_optim`.
593	    """
594	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
595	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint is not a valid document")
596	    migrated = {}
597	    try:
598	        params = document["params"]
599	        grads = document["grads"]
600	        hidden = document["hidden"]
601	        layers = document["layers"]
602	        pending = document["pending"]
603	    except KeyError as exc:
604	        raise CheckpointError(
605	            f"v1 checkpoint is missing field {exc.args[0]!r}; refusing to migrate"
606	        ) from None
607	    if not isinstance(params, list) or not isinstance(grads, list):
608	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint tensor lists are malformed")
609	    if len(params) != len(grads):
610	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint param/gradient counts disagree")
611	    m_params = []
612	    m_grads = []
613	    for index, (p_entry, g_entry) in enumerate(zip(params, grads)):
614	        m_params.append(_migrate_v1_entry(p_entry, f"parameter {index}"))
615	        m_grads.append(_migrate_v1_entry(g_entry, f"gradient {index}"))
616	        if m_params[-1]["s"] != m_grads[-1]["s"]:
617	            raise CheckpointError(
618	                f"v1 parameter {index} and its gradient disagree on shape"
619	            )
620	    migrated["params"] = m_params
621	    migrated["grads"] = m_grads
622	    if hidden is None:
623	        migrated["hidden"] = None
624	    else:
625	        if not isinstance(hidden, list) or not hidden:
626	            raise CheckpointError("v1 hidden state must be a non-empty list or null")
627	        migrated["hidden"] = [
628	            _migrate_v1_entry(entry, f"hidden slot {index}")
629	            for index, entry in enumerate(hidden)
630	        ]
631	    if not isinstance(layers, list) or not layers:
632	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint must record the layer order")
633	    m_layers = []
634	    for index, layer in enumerate(layers):
635	        _exact_keys(layer, _LAYER_KEYS, f"v1 layer {index} descriptor")
636	        kind = layer["kind"]
637	        if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
638	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 layer {index} kind must be a non-empty string")
639	        shapes = layer["shapes"]
640	        if not isinstance(shapes, list):
641	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 layer {index} shapes must be a list")
642	        m_shapes = []
643	        for shape in shapes:
644	            _check_shape(shape)
645	            m_shapes.append(list(shape))
646	        m_layers.append({"kind": kind, "shapes": m_shapes})
647	    migrated["layers"] = m_layers
648	    if not isinstance(pending, bool):
649	        raise CheckpointError("v1 pending flag must be a boolean")
650	    migrated["pending"] = pending
651	    if sum(len(layer["shapes"]) for layer in m_layers) != len(m_params):
652	        raise CheckpointError("v1 layer parameter counts do not match the parameter list")
653	    return migrated
654

656	def _migrate_add_optim(document):
657	    """Bring a pre-v3 document up to the current shape, item by item.
658	
659	    Versions 1 and 2 predate the optimizer state, so migration fixes the
660	    starting values exactly: step count ``t = 0`` and one zero first/second
661	    moment per parameter tensor.  The re-saved state is native version 3.
662	    """
663	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
664	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint is not a valid document")
665	    if document.get("optim") is not None:
666	        return document
667	    params = document.get("params")
668	    if not isinstance(params, list):
669	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint parameter list is malformed")
670	    m_entries = []
671	    v_entries = []
672	    for index, entry in enumerate(params):
673	        _exact_keys(entry, {"s", "v"}, f"parameter {index} entry")
674	        shape = entry["s"]
675	        _check_shape(shape)
676	        m_entries.append({"s": list(shape), "v": _zeros_tree(shape)})
677	        v_entries.append({"s": list(shape), "v": _zeros_tree(shape)})
678	    document["optim"] = {"t": 0, "m": m_entries, "v": v_entries}
679	    return document

682	def _migrate_v1_entry(entry, what):
683	    _exact_keys(entry, {"s", "v"}, f"v1 {what} entry")
684	    shape = entry["s"]
685	    _check_shape(shape)
686	    tree = entry["v"]
687	    if not _shape_matches(tree, shape):
688	        raise CheckpointError(f"v1 {what} values do not match their declared shape")
689	    # Re-walk the leaves so oversized integers / non-finite values smuggled
690	    # into a v1 payload are refused during migration, not after applying.
691	    _validate_migrated_tree(tree, shape, what)
692	    return {"s": list(shape), "v": _copy_tree(tree)}
693	
694	
695	def _validate_migrated_tree(tree, shape, what):
696	    if shape:
697	        if not isinstance(tree, list) or len(tree) != shape[0]:
698	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 {what} values do not match their declared shape")
699	        for item in tree:
700	            _validate_migrated_tree(item, shape[1:], what)
701	    else:
702	        if isinstance(tree, list):
703	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 {what} values do not match their declared shape")
704	        _check_leaf(tree)
705	
706	
707	def _copy_tree(tree):
708	    if isinstance(tree, list):
709	        return [_copy_tree(item) for item in tree]
710	    return tree
711	
712	
713	def _zeros_tree(shape):
714	    if not shape:
715	        return 0.0
716	    return [_zeros_tree(shape[1:]) for _ in range(shape[0])]
717

719	def _check_step_count(value, what="optimizer step count"):
720	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
721	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} must be a non-negative integer")
722	    if value > _INT64_MAX:
723	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} is too large to represent (int64)")
724	    return value

746	def _freeze_delta(document, schema_shapes):
747	    """Build delta framing from ``{b,n,hc,changed,pending}``.
748	
749	    *schema_shapes* maps the flat tensor index of every tensor the
750	    post-delta state may contain to its shape: params then grads then the
751	    (newly introduced, if any) hidden slots.
752	    """
753	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
754	        raise CheckpointError("delta document must be an object")
755	    _exact_keys(document, _DELTA_HEADER_KEYS, "delta header")
756	    if document["v"] != FORMAT_VERSION:
757	        raise CheckpointError("delta version must be the current format version")
758	    basis_name = document["b"]
759	    if not isinstance(basis_name, str) or basis_name != _segment_name(_BASIS_INDEX):
760	        raise CheckpointError("delta must name its basis segment")
761	    number = document["n"]
762	    if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, int) or number <= 0:
763	        raise CheckpointError("delta segment number must be a positive int")
764	    hc = document["hc"]
765	    if hc is not None and (isinstance(hc, bool) or not isinstance(hc, int) or hc < 0):
766	        raise CheckpointError("delta hidden count must be a non-negative int or null")
767	    changed = document["changed"]
768	    if not isinstance(changed, list):
769	        raise CheckpointError("delta changed list must be a list")
770	    if not isinstance(document["pending"], bool):
771	        raise CheckpointError("pending flag must be a boolean")
772	
773	    payload = []
774	    seen = set()
775	    header_entries = []
776	    previous_index = -1
777	    for position, entry in enumerate(changed):
778	        _exact_keys(entry, _CHANGED_INPUT_KEYS, f"delta changed entry {position}")
779	        index = entry["i"]
780	        if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
781	            raise CheckpointError(f"delta changed entry {position} has a bad index")
782	        if index in seen:
783	            raise CheckpointError(f"delta lists tensor {index} more than once")
784	        if index <= previous_index:
785	            raise CheckpointError("delta changed entries must be strictly ordered")
786	        previous_index = index
787	        seen.add(index)
788	        shape = entry["s"]
789	        _check_shape(shape)
790	        if index >= len(schema_shapes):
791	            raise CheckpointError(
792	                f"delta changed entry {position} names a tensor beyond the model"
793	            )
794	        if list(shape) != schema_shapes[index]:
795	            raise CheckpointError(
796	                f"delta changed entry {position} shape does not match the chain"
797	            )
798	        tree = entry["v"]
799	        if not _shape_matches(tree, shape):
800	            raise CheckpointError("delta tensor tree does not match its declared shape")
801	        _freeze_tree(tree, shape, payload)
802	        header_entries.append({"i": index, "s": list(shape)})
803	
804	    header = {
805	        "v": FORMAT_VERSION,
806	        "b": basis_name,
807	        "n": number,
808	        "hc": hc,
809	        "changed": header_entries,
810	        "pending": document["pending"],
811	    }
812	    return _frame(DELTA_MAGIC, DELTA_END_MAGIC, header, payload)

815	def _parse_delta(raw, segment_index_expected):
816	    """Validate one delta segment and return ``(number, hc, pending, items)``.
817	
818	    *items* is a list of ``(flat_index, shape, tree)`` already decoded.
819	    """
820	    if not isinstance(raw, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
821	        raise CheckpointError("delta segment must be bytes")
822	    version, header, payload, leaf_count = _read_frame(
823	        bytes(raw), DELTA_MAGIC, DELTA_END_MAGIC, "delta segment"
824	    )
825	    if version not in SUPPORTED_DELTA_VERSIONS:
826	        raise CheckpointError(
827	            f"delta segments must be version {SUPPORTED_DELTA_VERSIONS}, "
828	            f"got {version}"
829	        )
830	    _exact_keys(header, _DELTA_HEADER_KEYS, "delta header")
831	    if header["v"] != version:
832	        raise CheckpointError("delta header version does not match")
833	    if header["b"] != _segment_name(_BASIS_INDEX):
834	        raise CheckpointError("delta does not name the chain's basis segment")
835	    number = header["n"]
836	    if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, int) or number <= 0:
837	        raise CheckpointError("delta segment number must be a positive int")
838	    if number != segment_index_expected:
839	        raise CheckpointError(
840	            f"delta segment number {number} does not match its position "
841	            f"{segment_index_expected} in the chain"
842	        )
843	    hc = header["hc"]
844	    if hc is not None and (isinstance(hc, bool) or not isinstance(hc, int) or hc < 0):
845	        raise CheckpointError("delta hidden count must be a non-negative int or null")
846	    changed = header["changed"]
847	    if not isinstance(changed, list):
848	        raise CheckpointError("delta changed list must be a list")
849	    if not isinstance(header["pending"], bool):
850	        raise CheckpointError("pending flag must be a boolean")
851	
852	    total_leaves = 0
853	    seen = set()
854	    descriptors = []
855	    previous_index = -1
856	    for position, entry in enumerate(changed):
857	        _exact_keys(entry, _CHANGED_KEYS, f"delta changed entry {position}")
858	        index = entry["i"]
859	        if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
860	            raise CheckpointError(f"delta changed entry {position} has a bad index")
861	        if index in seen or index <= previous_index:
862	            raise CheckpointError(
863	                f"delta changed entry {position} is duplicated or out of order"
864	            )
865	        seen.add(index)
866	        previous_index = index
867	        shape = entry["s"]
868	        _check_shape(shape)
869	        total_leaves += _shape_size(shape)
870	        descriptors.append((index, list(shape)))
871	    if total_leaves != leaf_count:
872	        raise CheckpointError("delta leaf count does not match its changed tensors")
873	
874	    reader = _LeafReader(payload)
875	    items = [
876	        (index, shape, reader.tree(shape)) for index, shape in descriptors
877	    ]
878	    if reader.remaining() != 0:
879	        raise CheckpointError("delta payload has trailing bytes")
880	    return number, hc, header["pending"], items

888	def _tensors_from_document(document):
889	    """Return ``{flat_index: (shape, tree)}`` for one full state document.
890	
891	    The flat index space is: parameters, gradients, optimizer first
892	    moments, optimizer second moments, the optimizer step count (a scalar),
893	    then the hidden slots.  Hidden slots come last so introducing hidden
894	    state mid-chain only ever appends new indices.
895	    """
896	    tensors = {}
897	    offset = 0
898	    for entry in document["params"]:
899	        tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
900	        offset += 1
901	    for entry in document["grads"]:
902	        tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
903	        offset += 1
904	    optim = document["optim"]
905	    for entry in optim["m"]:
906	        tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
907	        offset += 1
908	    for entry in optim["v"]:
909	        tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
910	        offset += 1
911	    tensors[offset] = ([], optim["t"])
912	    offset += 1
913	    hidden = document["hidden"]
914	    if hidden is not None:
915	        for entry in hidden:
916	            tensors[offset] = (entry["s"], entry["v"])
917	            offset += 1
918	    return tensors
919

921	def _flat_hidden_base(param_count):
922	    """First flat index of the hidden slots for *param_count* parameters."""
923	    return 4 * param_count + 1
924

926	def _trees_differ(a, b, shape):
927	    if shape:
928	        if not isinstance(a, list) or not isinstance(b, list):
929	            return True
930	        if len(a) != shape[0] or len(b) != shape[0]:
931	            return True
932	        return any(
933	            _trees_differ(x, y, shape[1:]) for x, y in zip(a, b)
934	        )
935	    if isinstance(a, list) or isinstance(b, list):
936	        return True
937	    return _leaf_code(a) != _leaf_code(b)

940	def _assemble(basis_document, applied):
941	    """Build a full document from basis tensors plus per-index replacements.
942	
943	    *applied* maps a flat tensor index (params, grads, optimizer moments,
944	    step count, then hidden) to ``(shape, tree)``.  Hidden indices only
945	    exist once a delta introduced hidden state; a complete set must be
946	    present at that point.
947	    """
948	    param_count = len(basis_document["params"])
949	    layers = basis_document["layers"]
950	    hidden_count = len(basis_document["hidden"]) if basis_document["hidden"] is not None else None
951	
952	    # The latest delta in the chain decides whether hidden state exists.
953	    final_hidden_count = applied.get("_hc", hidden_count)
954	    tensors = applied["tensors"]
955	
956	    hidden_base = _flat_hidden_base(param_count)
957	    total = hidden_base + (final_hidden_count or 0)
958	    for index in range(total):
959	        if index not in tensors:
960	            raise CheckpointError(
961	                f"chain is missing tensor {index}: the delta chain is incomplete"
962	            )
963	
964	    def entries(start, stop):
965	        return [
966	            {"s": list(tensors[i][0]), "v": tensors[i][1]}
967	            for i in range(start, stop)
968	        ]
969	
970	    params = entries(0, param_count)
971	    grads = entries(param_count, 2 * param_count)
972	    optim_m = entries(2 * param_count, 3 * param_count)
973	    optim_v = entries(3 * param_count, 4 * param_count)
974	    step_shape, step_count = tensors[4 * param_count]
975	    if step_shape != []:
976	        raise CheckpointError("optimizer step count tensor must be a scalar")
977	    _check_step_count(step_count)
978	    hidden = entries(hidden_base, total)
979	
980	    if len(params) != param_count or len(grads) != param_count:
981	        raise CheckpointError("chain did not preserve the parameter/gradient count")
982	    return {
983	        "params": params,
984	        "grads": grads,
985	        "hidden": hidden if final_hidden_count is not None else None,
986	        "optim": {"t": step_count, "m": optim_m, "v": optim_v},
